Geographic focus:
Americas (United States, Venezuela); secondary reference to global oil markets

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report YES (covers SPR drawdowns, past exchanges, prior administration denials)
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) YES (swap mechanics being actively discussed, "topping out" process said to begin shortly)
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) YES (SPR refill trajectory, cavern integrity concerns, refinery investment requirements)

Synopsis:
Following a US-Venezuela deal, the Trump administration is exploring a crude swap arrangement to replenish the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, now at a 44-year low after major releases during the Iran war. Venezuelan heavy, high-sulfur crude (Merey-16, Boscan) is technically incompatible with SPR quality specifications, so a direct injection is not feasible. Energy Secretary Wright floated a swap: Venezuelan heavy crude exchanged for US light/medium crude which would then enter the SPR. However, US refinery appetite for additional Venezuelan heavy barrels is constrained by specialized processing unit capacity. The article is primarily an oil market story about SPR logistics, crude quality mismatches, and geopolitical energy diplomacy.
